 :Judgment:
This petition emanates from the Motor Vehicle Accident dated 26.05.2023 wherein the petitioners
have sought for compensation with respect to the death of Nanjunda due to the impact of the
accident.
2.

Succinctly stated the facts germane to the lis involved in this petition are briefly summarized as follows:
It is the case of the petitioners that the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the parents of deceased Nanjunda who died in the Road Traffic Accident on 26.05.2023 due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the respondent's mini bus.

It is submitted that on 26.05.2023 at about 12.50 a.m., when Nanjunda was riding the TVS XL Heavy Duty bearing Reg.No.KA- 10-EA-1039 from Begur towards Basavanna Circle slowly, carefully and following traffic rules and regulations and when he reached near Radiant Redwood Apartment, Begur - Koppa road, Bengaluru,
at that time, the respondent's Swaraj Mazda Mini bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-A-8318 was driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed Rakshitha vs The Partner Megha Travels on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170601852/
2 against the SCCH 15 4 MVC No.7530/2023 motorcycle of Nanjunda.

sentences.text: Due to this impact, he fell down and sustained severe injuries all over the body.

Immediately after the accident Nanjunda was shifted to nearby Jayashree hospital,
after first aid treatment he was shifted to Forties hospital.
Then shifted to Victoria hospital, but he died while under treatment on 26.05.2023 at about 9.10 p.m.

Consequently, on 26.05.2023 a FIR No.0092/2023 was registered with the Hulimavu Traffic Police station under Sec.279 and 337 of IPC and charge sheet was filed under Sec.279, 304(A) of IPC and under Sec.3(1), 181, 5,180, 146, 196 of IMV act.
The Petitioners submit that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the mini bus.

It is submitted that the deceased was hale and healthy and aged about 30 years and doing Chemical and Phenyl business and earning Rs.1,500/- per day and he was the sole bread earner and had good future prospects.

Due to untimely death of the deceased the Petitioners have lost love,
affection and support which has caused mental agony to the petitioners.
Hence, the petitioners have claimed compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with costs and interest at SCCH 15 5 MVC No.7530/2023 the rate of 12% p.a in the interest of justice and equity.
3. In pursuance of service of notice issued to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 has remained absent and he was placed exparte.

Respondent No.2 filed Written Statement contending as follows:
The respondent No.2 admitted that it has issued insurance policy to the offending Swaraj Mazda Mini bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 42-A-8318 in favour of the respondent No.1.
Without prejudice the liability of the respondent No.2 if any is subject to the validity of driving license and terms and conditions of the insurance policy.
The driver of the said bus did not have valid and effective driving license.
It is denied that the accident took place due to the negligent driving of the driver of the bus.
It is submitted that the alleged accident took place due to the sole negligence of the deceased.
The age, avocation of the deceased is denied.
Hence, on these grounds Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that Sri. V. Nanjunda S/o Venkatarama was died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 26.05.2023 at about 12.50 a.m., on Pushpapura Village, Shagya Post, Hanur Taluk, Chamarajanagara District, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Swaraj Mazda Mini Bus bearing Rakshitha vs The Partner Megha Travels on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170601852/
3 Reg.No.KA-42- A-8318?
2) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Sri. V. Nanjunda?
3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?
4) What Order or Award ?

5. In order to substantiate the claim petition, the claimants have examined petitioner No.1 as PW1 and and examined one witness as PW.2 and relied upon Ex.P.1 to 17 documents and the Respondent No.2 got examined two witnesses as RW.1 and 2 and SCCH 15 7 MVC No.7530/2023 relied upon Ex.R1 and 2 documents.

Having perused the records my issue wise findings run as under:-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative. Issue No.4 : As per the Final Order for the following :
REASONS 7. Issue No.1:
Before adjudication of the issue with respect to the compensation it is quintessential to adjudicate on the issue of negligence.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Swaraj Mazda Mini bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-A-8318 (herein after referred to as the offending vehicle).
8.

In this regard the petitioner No 1 has got herself examined as PW1 and in her chief examination she has deposed that on SCCH 15 8 MVC No.7530/2023 26.05.2023 at about 6.30 a.m., the deceased was riding TVS XL Heavy Duty bearing Reg.No.KA-10-EA-1039 from Begur towards Basavanna circle slowly, cautiously and observing all the traffic rules and regulations and when he reached Radiant Redwood Apartment at that time offending vehicle was driven in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed against the deceased's motorcycle resulting in the accident and death of the motorist.
9.

It is elicited in the charge sheet that the complainant who is the police official has witnessed the accident and given his evidence independently as PW2 and the accident occurred when he was patrolling duty in the bolero Jeep bearing Reg No KA-02-G- 1513.

In the course of investigation it is elicited that the accident occurred at about 12.50 mid night near Red wood Apartment front road and motor cycle was going from Begur towards Basavanna Circle and the mini bus which was coming from Basavanna Circle dashed the motor cycle and caused the accident resulting in the death of the motorist and later mini bus driver took his bus to the left side and it rubbed the right Rakshitha vs The Partner Megha Travels on 6 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/170601852/
4 side door of the police jeep.

10. As far as the manner of the accident is concerned Pw1 is cross examined by the learned counsel for the respondent No 2 and she has admitted that the police have filed charge sheet against her husband for not having DL and insurance to the motor cycle.
PW1 has deposed that the bike driven by her husband belongs to one Venkatarama and the police have also filed charge sheet against him for not having insurance to his motor cycle.

It is suggested by the learned counsel for the respondent no 2 that even though the accident has taken place due to the negligence and rash driving of the deceased since the deceased did not have DL as well as insurance in collusion with the police a false complaint is given against the bus driver.
11.
In order to prove the manner of the accident the complainant who lodged complaint who was on patrolling duty at that place and an eye witness is examined as PW2.

He has deposed that they had parked their jeep at the left side near Red wood Apartment and saw that the swaraj mazda bus dashed the bike which was coming from its front side and took bus to left side SCCH 15 10 MVC No.7530/2023 and rubbed to the right side door of the jeep.
In his cross examination PW2 has denied that the accident took place due to the negligence of the bike rider.

12. As far as the accident is concerned respondent No 2 has got examined the driver of the offending vehicle/bus and he has deposed that the deceased motorist himself came from the front side in a Zig Zag manner and in an inebriated condition and dashed the bus in the front side resulting in the accident and he tried to prevent the accident but the accident was inevitable consequence and in the process he dashed the front door of the police jeep.

However when cross examined by the learned counsel for the petitioner he has admitted that he has crossed the white mark on the road and also admitted that he saw the bike from a distance of 30 feet in which case he would have certainly avoided the accident if he was driving slowly.
It is due to the fact that the bus rider was in high speed that he could not avoid the accident.
In addition if it was a case of contributory negligence then nothing prevented the police to file charge sheet against drivers of both the vehicles.

sentences.text: If the observations made in these decisions is taken into consideration it can be gathered from the evidence that the bus has dashed the bike from front side and the bike was coming from the opposite direction hence it is not a case of mere involvement of the bus in the accident on the other hand the bus could have SCCH 15 12 MVC No.7530/2023 avoided the accident if it was not driven in high speed.
In addition apart from the charge sheet the complainant who is the eye witness is examined in this case and the bus driver has also given evidence in this case.
Merely because the deceased did not have driving license is by itself not a ground to hold that the deceased has contributed to the accident.
In addition it is not mentioned anywhere that the deceased had consumed alcohol or evidence to prove drunken driving by the deceased.
Hence the oral and documentary evidence discloses that the accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle/bus.
Hence I answer Issue no 1 in favour of the petitioners and in the Affirmative.
14. Issue No.2: It is stated in the Petition as well as in the evidence of PW.1 that the Petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioner No.2 and 3 are the parents of the deceased Nanjunda.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, PW.1 has relied on Ex.P9, 10 and 12 i.e., the Aadhaar cards of the Petitioner No.1 and deceased and election ID of petitioner No.2.
The same shows the relationship between the Petitioners and the deceased.

Hence, they have a right SCCH 15 13 MVC No.7530/2023 to apply for compensation due to death of Nanjunda in RTA.
15.

In the case of Seema Rani & Ors. v. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors 2025 the Supreme Court reiterated that the major, married, and earning children of a deceased victim, as the legal representatives, have the right to apply for motor accident compensation.

Birender (2020), wherein it was expounded that "major married and earning sons of the deceased, being legal representatives, have a right to apply for compensation, and the Tribunal must consider the application, irrespective of whether the representatives are fully dependent on the deceased or not."

16. The Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the father and mother of the deceased,
being the legal representatives of deceased Nanjunda have a right to apply for compensation.

As the Petitioners are the LRs of deceased Nanjunda and also they have proved that the death of the Nanjunda has been caused by rash and negligent driving of the SCCH 15 14 MVC No.7530/2023 driver of the offending vehicle, they are entitled for the compensation.
Hence I answer Issue No 2 in the Affirmative.

17. Issue No.3: Computation of compensation under the various heads is assessed as follows:
1. Loss of dependency Age factor:
In order to assess the compensation under the head of loss of dependency the age, avocation and income of the deceased needs to be ascertained.
In the present case, the age of the deceased is shown as 30 years.
Ex.P-10 is the Aadhaar card which shows that the date of birth of the deceased is 01.01.1993.

Hence, by considering Ex.P10, the age of the deceased is taken as 30 years.
18. Income and avocation:
It is stated in the evidence that deceased was a chemical and phenol seller and was earning Rs.1,500/- per month.
The Petitioners have not produced any documentary evidence to prove the actual income of the deceased.
Hence in the absence of evidence to prove the actual income of the SCCH 15 15 MVC No.7530/2023 deceased the notional income will have to be taken into consideration.
Looking into the age of the deceased and the avocation it is just and proper to fix the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,000/- per month.
Therefore, the Annual Income of the deceased would be 16,000X 12= 1,92,000/-.

Hence for the purpose of computation of claim,
the annual income of the deceased is taken as Rs.1,92,000/-.
19.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Sarla Verma v. DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121 has established the golden principles in considering compensation in cases of death.

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Relevant part of the judgment at paras 18- 19 is reproduced hereunder:
"18.

The criteria which are to be taken into consideration for assessing compensation in the case of death are: (i) the age of the deceased at the time of his death; (ii) the number of dependents left behind by the deceased; and (iii) the income of the deceased at the time of his death.
There will
be lesser need for detailed evidence.
It will be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
"Step 1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand) The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance, which is considered to be the contribution to the dependant family, constitutes the multiplicand.

Step 2 (Ascertaining the multiplier)

sentences.text: This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a Table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said Table with reference to the age of the deceased."

Moving forward with the Point of future prospects, the Constitution Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi reported as (2017) 16 SCC 680, held that Future prospects are to be awarded on the basis of:
(i) The nature of the deceased's employment; and (ii) The age of the deceased.
SCCH 15 17 MVC No.7530/2023 Relying on Para 59.4 of Pranay Sethi (supra), while determining the income, an addition of 40% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects should be made, where the deceased is self- employed and was below the age of 40 years.

sentences.text: At the time of the death of the deceased, he was survived by his wife, father and mother.
Hence while calculating the deductions towards the personal expenses, the number of dependents at the time of the death of the deceased is to be considered.

As per the dicta of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India was pleased to hold that where the number of dependents of family members is 2 to 3, 1/3rd of the income of the deceased may be deducted towards his personal and living expenses.
21. In this Petition, the deceased was aged 30 years at the time of accident.
Hence, towards future prospects 40% of the income has to be added.
So, 40% of Rs.16,000/- comes to Rs.6,400/-.

Therefore, the income of the deceased comes to Rs.22,400/- p.m. (Rs.16,000/- + Rs.6,400/- =
Rs.22,400/-).

Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport SCCH 15 18 MVC No.7530/2023 Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 17.

22. After deducting 1/3rd of the income towards his personal expenses in Rs.22,400/- it comes to Rs.14,934/- (22,400/- - 7,466/-) and multiplier applied is 17, (Rs.14,934/- x 12 = 1,79,208/-,
Rs.1,79,208/- x 17 = 30,46,536/-).
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.30,46,536/- towards loss of dependency.

sentences.text: Loss of Estate, Loss of Consortium' and 'Funeral Expenses'

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi (Supra), the conventional heads, namely, 'Loss of Estate',
Loss of Consortium' and 'Funeral Expenses', SCCH 15 19 MVC No.7530/2023 amount of compensation is fixed as Rs. 15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs. 15,000/-, respectively with an increase of 10% after a period of 3 years.
It is further observed in the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.

By applying the said observation made in the aforesaid case, since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Further, the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/- each.

In view of the decision in United India Insurance Company Limited Vs Satinder Kaur Alias Satwinder Kaur and Ors. (2021) 11 SCC 780, no compensation is to be granted under the head 'Loss of Love and Affection'.

26. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the negligent parking of the Swaraj Mazda Mini bus bearing Reg.No.KA-42-A- 8318.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1 and has to pay compensation amount to the Petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
27. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation of Rs.32,28,036/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.
In the result, I proceed to pass the SCCH 15 22 MVC No.7530/2023 following :
ORDER The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.32,28,036/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

This petition emanates from the Motor Vehicle Accident dated 26.05.2023 wherein the petitioners
have sought for compensation with respect to the death of Nanjunda due to the impact of the
accident.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
If the observations made in these decisions is taken into consideration it can be gathered from the evidence that the bus has dashed the bike from front side and the bike was coming from the opposite direction hence it is not a case of mere involvement of the bus in the accident on the other hand the bus could have SCCH 15 12 MVC No.7530/2023 avoided the accident if it was not driven in high speed.
In addition apart from the charge sheet the complainant who is the eye witness is examined in this case and the bus driver has also given evidence in this case.
Merely because the deceased did not have driving license is by itself not a ground to hold that the deceased has contributed to the accident.
In addition it is not mentioned anywhere that the deceased had consumed alcohol or evidence to prove drunken driving by the deceased.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Hence, they have a right SCCH 15 13 MVC No.7530/2023 to apply for compensation due to death of Nanjunda in RTA.
15.
In the case of Seema Rani & Ors. v. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors 2025 the Supreme Court reiterated that the major, married, and earning children of a deceased victim, as the legal representatives, have the right to apply for motor accident compensation.
16. The Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 and 3 are the father and mother of the deceased,
being the legal representatives of deceased Nanjunda have a right to apply for compensation.
As the Petitioners are the LRs of deceased Nanjunda and also they have proved that the death of the Nanjunda has been caused by rash and negligent driving of the SCCH 15 14 MVC No.7530/2023 driver of the offending vehicle, they are entitled for the compensation.
In the present case, the age of the deceased is shown as 30 years.
The alleged accident has taken place on 26.05.2023.
The Petitioners have not produced any documentary evidence to prove the actual income of the deceased.
Hence in the absence of evidence to prove the actual income of the SCCH 15 15 MVC No.7530/2023 deceased the notional income will have to be taken into consideration.
Looking into the age of the deceased and the avocation it is just and proper to fix the notional income of the deceased as Rs.16,000/- per month.
Therefore, the Annual Income of the deceased would be 16,000X 12= 1,92,000/-.
Hence for the purpose of computation of claim,
the annual income of the deceased is taken as Rs.1,92,000/-.
19.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Sarla Verma v. DTC, reported as (2009) 6 SCC 121 has established the golden principles in considering compensation in cases of death.
Hence while calculating the deductions towards the personal expenses, the number of dependents at the time of the death of the deceased is to be considered.
Further, as per the principles laid down in decision reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121 (Sarla Verma and Others Vs. Delhi Transport SCCH 15 18 MVC No.7530/2023 Corporation and another) the multiplier applicable is 17.
In view of the decision in United India Insurance Company Limited Vs Satinder Kaur Alias Satwinder Kaur and Ors. (2021) 11 SCC 780, no compensation is to be granted under the head 'Loss of Love and Affection'.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Thus, the Petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.30,46,536/- towards loss of dependency.
Hence the actual medical expenses incurred for the treatment of the deceased or any hospital charges are taken an Nil.
In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranay Sethi (Supra), the conventional heads, namely, 'Loss of Estate',
Loss of Consortium' and 'Funeral Expenses', SCCH 15 19 MVC No.7530/2023 amount of compensation is fixed as Rs. 15,000/-, Rs.40,000/- and Rs. 15,000/-, respectively with an increase of 10% after a period of 3 years.
It is further observed in the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.
By applying the said observation made in the aforesaid case, since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Further, the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/- each.
In light of the above discussion, the claimants are awarded compensation as follows:

Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1 and has to pay compensation amount to the Petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
27. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation of Rs.32,28,036/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.
In the result, I proceed to pass the SCCH 15 22 MVC No.7530/2023 following :
ORDER The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.32,28,036/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are apportioned among them are as shown below:
